caption:
🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Monday, 9 November 2026

1. 💷 Council opens £250 cost of living grant applications to some Surrey residents
Applications for household grants of up to £250 are opening to some Surrey residents. The grants are part of the council's cost of living help.

2. ⚡ Government's EV targets are expected to be cut this week
New petrol and diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030, and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission. The targets are expected to be reduced this week.

3. 🏥 Burnham unveils £40m to keep patients out of hospital
Burnham admitted the NHS faces a difficult winter. Health secretary Yvette Cooper said it had already had a "heavy summer" as a result of a series of heatwaves.

4. 🏠 Burnham's pledge to get everyone in for Christmas is in jeopardy
Official figures show nearly 1,000 more people sleeping rough in England between January and June. A minister cited a chronic housing shortage as Labour hopes to offer a bed to every rough sleeper.

5. ☕ Starbucks plans to hire 7,500 baristas over the next five years
The chain is targeting growth north of London with 500 extra outlets, in a boost to youth employment. The US coffee shop chain employs more than 18,000 people in the UK.

6. 🌫️ Dense fog could disrupt Monday morning's rush hour
Fog could disrupt the commute on Monday morning.

7. 📚 Secondary schools are told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10
The government says pupils in Years 7 to 9 should have "richer, more engaging" learning than preparing for GCSEs.

8. 🏥 Only 6.4% of stroke survivors receive enough therapy, report finds
Fewer than one in 15 stroke survivors get the amount of therapy the NHS should provide to maximise recovery. The Stroke Association called the report "damning" and says the lack of rehabilitation hinders patients' recovery.

Sources: BBC, Guardian. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Lauren Hurley / No 10 Downing Street / OGL 3, Wikimedia Commons; Prime Minister's Office / OGL 3, Wikimedia Commons.
